(1) the inversion of a MOS capacitor can be achieved under low illumination conditions, (2) the frequency dependency of the capacitance-voltage curves under illumination can be described by a model, and (3) the current-voltage characteristics under illumination can be used to determine the photogenerated carriers in a MOS capacitor.
the MOS capacitance under illumination is a powerful tool to characterize the MOS structure and to determine the photogenerated carriers in MOS devices.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of MOS devices under illumination.
the development of new characterization methods of MOS structures and devices under illumination.
the investigation of MOS structures under illumination and the extraction of photogeneration parameters from the I-V characteristics.

C-V measurements are a powerful and reliable tool for MOS characterization, while the extraction of carrier densities from I-V measurements is not straightforward and requires careful considerations.
